mainTopic: The time limits for overcharging (אונאה) claims, learned from the merchants of לוד and settled by רבא, with רב נחמן limiting the deadline to the buyer.
overview: The משנה tells that רבי טרפון ruled in לוד that אונאה (overcharging) goes up to one-third, and the merchants were happy. When he added that the buyer can back out all day, they went back to the view of the חכמים. The גמרא first finishes a proof from this story: under the רבנן, a small overcharge is forgiven only after the time it takes to show the item to a merchant or relative. That proof is pushed back. The גמרא then uses the merchants' happiness to ask whether a sale cancelled for an overcharge of more than one-sixth can be undone forever, and that proof is pushed back too. רבא rules the final הלכה: less than one-sixth, the sale stands; exactly one-sixth, the extra money is returned; more than one-sixth, the sale is cancelled. Both claims must be made within the short checking time, and a ברייתא supports him. Finally, רב נחמן says this time limit applies only to the buyer, and the גמרא begins to bring support for him from the merchants of לוד.

steps.title: Finishing the proof that the רבנן do not forgive small overcharges right away
steps.stepSummary: If both the רבנן and רבי טרפון forgave small overcharges immediately, the merchants would have had no reason to go back to the רבנן, because רבי טרפון's view would have been better for them. So the proof concludes that under the רבנן a small overcharge is forgiven only after the time to show the item to a merchant or relative.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if according to רבי טרפון too a small overcharge is forgiven right away, why did the merchants go back to the רבנן? רבי טרפון's view would suit them better, since an overcharge the רבנן call אונאה is forgiven according to רבי טרפון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof it started just before this section. It wants to show that under the רבנן, an overcharge of less than one-sixth is not forgiven immediately, but only after the buyer has had time to show the item to a merchant or relative.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works by elimination. If both opinions forgave small overcharges immediately, רבי טרפון would simply be better for sellers, because he forgives even exactly one-sixth. Since the merchants still went back to the רבנן, there must be a difference in timing: under the רבנן the buyer can complain only for the short showing time, while רבי טרפון gives him 'all day.'

keyTerms.meaning: forgiveness of the overcharge; the deal stands with nothing to pay back
overcharging; the deal stands but the extra money is paid back

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Tarfon too
phrases.notes: This continues a line just before this text: 'if you say that for the רבנן a small overcharge is forgiven right away...'

phrases.english: there is forgiveness immediately,
why did they go back?
phrases.notes: The merchants of לוד went back to the view of the חכמים, as the משנה says.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon's view would suit them better,
since what the Rabbis
treat as overcharging
is forgiven according to Rabbi Tarfon?
phrases.notes: He means an overcharge of exactly one-sixth.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן נָמֵי לְאַלְתַּר הָוְיָא מְחִילָה, אַמַּאי חָזְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a proof attempt begun before this section of the daf.
steps.raayaObject: Under the רבנן, an overcharge of less than one-sixth is forgiven only after the time it takes to show the item to a merchant or relative, not immediately.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's story that the merchants of לוד went back to the חכמים after hearing 'all day.'

steps.title: The ranges do not line up the way the proof assumed
steps.stepSummary: The proof wrongly compared רבי טרפון's 'less than a third' to the רבנן's 'less than a sixth.' In fact, from one-sixth to one-third under רבי טרפון is like exactly one-sixth under the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think that less than a third for רבי טרפון is like less than a sixth for the רבנן? No. From a sixth up to a third for רבי טרפון is like exactly a sixth for the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. It corrects how the two opinions match up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed that everything under one-third was simply forgiven for רבי טרפון. In fact, the range from one-sixth to one-third is real אונאה for him: the deal stands, but the money is paid back. So 'all day' applies to claiming money back in that range, and the story says nothing about how quickly the רבנן forgive small overcharges.

keyTerms.meaning: do you think? (an opening that pushes back on an assumption)

steps.confusionAlert: Under the רבנן there are three levels. Less than one-sixth is forgiven. Exactly one-sixth is אונאה, so money is paid back. More than one-sixth cancels the sale. Keep these three apart.

phrases.english: Do you think
that less than a third for Rabbi Tarfon
is like less than a sixth for the Rabbis?
No,
from a sixth up to a third for Rabbi Tarfon
is like exactly a sixth for the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי סָבְרַתְּ פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁלִישׁ לְרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן כְּפָחוֹת מִשְּׁתוּת לְרַבָּנַן דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 1 by correcting its assumption.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the merchants going back.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed that רבי טרפון's whole range below one-third was forgiven, when the part from one-sixth to one-third is actually אונאה.

steps.title: Then why were the merchants happy at first?
steps.stepSummary: If the range from one-sixth to one-third under רבי טרפון is still אונאה, it is unclear what the merchants gained that made them happy at first.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what were they happy about at first?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rejection from step 2. It also sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the merchants rejoiced when they first heard רבי טרפון's ruling. If his ruling still makes the seller pay money back in that range, the גמרא asks what the advantage was. Finding that advantage will lead into the second open question.

phrases.english: If so,
what did they rejoice about at first?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection given in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 2 that one-sixth to one-third under רבי טרפון equals exactly one-sixth under the רבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If so, his ruling seems to give the sellers nothing extra, so their happiness makes no sense.

steps.title: Proof that under the רבנן a cancelled sale can always be undone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge by proving the second open question. Under the רבנן, a buyer whose overcharge cancels the sale can always back out. That explains why the merchants were happy at first and then went back.
steps.simpleTranslation: Resolve from here that cancelling a sale, according to the רבנן, can always be done. Once רבי טרפון told them the case is only אונאה, they were happy. When he told them 'all day,' they went back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the merchants' happiness to settle a different open question. It concludes that under the רבנן, the buyer can always cancel a sale when the overcharge is more than one-sixth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the רבנן, more than one-sixth cancels the sale. If that cancellation could happen at any time, then רבי טרפון calling the case only אונאה was a big gain for sellers: the sale stands, and the buyer has only a short time to complain. When רבי טרפון added that the buyer has all day, that gain shrank, so they went back.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is where the second open question about the רבנן seems to get an answer. Step 6 will push back on it.

phrases.english: Resolve
phrases.notes: Settle the other open question too: can a cancelled sale be undone any time, or only for a short while?

phrases.english: that cancelling a sale, for the Rabbis,
one can always back out,
for once Rabbi Tarfon told them
it is overcharging, they rejoiced;

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲמַר לְהוּ כׇּל הַיּוֹם – חָזְרוּ.
phrases.english: when he told them 'all day,' they went back.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּפְשׁוֹט דְּבִטּוּל מִקָּח לְרַבָּנַן לְעוֹלָם חוֹזֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3 and uses that answer to settle the second open question.
steps.raayaObject: Under the רבנן, a buyer can always back out of a sale cancelled by an overcharge of more than one-sixth.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The merchants' first happiness and their later return to the חכמים.

steps.title: Why the proof works
steps.stepSummary: If a cancelled sale under the רבנן could be undone only for a short time, רבי טרפון's ruling would give the merchants no advantage, so their happiness would make no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you thought that under the רבנן a sale could be cancelled only within the time it takes to show the item to a merchant or a relative, what would they have been happy about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the logic behind the proof in step 4 by showing that the other possibility does not fit the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If cancelling under the רבנן were also limited to the short showing period, then רבי טרפון's ruling would bring the sellers no clear benefit. Since they were happy, the cancellation under the רבנן must have no time limit.

keyTerms.meaning: if it entered your mind, if you would think
within the time it takes to show the item to a merchant

phrases.english: For if you would think
that cancelling a sale, for the Rabbis,
is only within the time to show it to a merchant or his relative,
what did they rejoice about?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ דְּבִטּוּל מִקָּח לְרַבָּנַן בִּכְדֵי שֶׁיַּרְאֶה לַתַּגָּר אוֹ לִקְרוֹבוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the proof in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: A cancelled sale under the רבנן has no time limit.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Elimination: a time limit would leave the merchants' happiness unexplained.

steps.title: They were happy about the exact one-sixth case
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The merchants' happiness can be explained by an overcharge of exactly one-sixth: רבי טרפון forgives it, while the רבנן call it אונאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They were happy about an overcharge of exactly one-sixth, which רבי טרפון forgives and the רבנן treat as אונאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from steps 4 and 5. It finds a different reason the merchants could have been happy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An overcharge of exactly one-sixth costs the seller money under the רבנן, but under רבי טרפון it is simply forgiven. That alone is a gain for sellers. So the story no longer proves anything about how long a cancelled sale can be undone. The גמרא raises this question formally in step 7, and רבא settles it in step 12.
steps.whatToRemember: Both attempts to answer questions about the רבנן from the story of the merchants of לוד are pushed back. Exactly one-sixth is the key case: רבי טרפון forgives it, while the רבנן require the money to be paid back.

phrases.english: They rejoiced over exactly a sixth,
which for Rabbi Tarfon is forgiven,
and for the Rabbis is overcharging.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׂמְחוּ בְּשֶׁתּוּת עַצְמָהּ, דִּלְרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן מְחִילָה, וּלְרַבָּנַן אוֹנָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof made in steps 4 and 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that a cancelled sale under the רבנן can always be undone.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The merchants' happiness has another explanation: exactly one-sixth is forgiven by רבי טרפון but must be paid back under the רבנן.

steps.title: How long can a cancelled sale be undone under the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether, under the רבנן, a sale cancelled for an overcharge of more than one-sixth can be undone forever, or only for the short time it takes to show the item to a merchant or relative.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: according to the רבנן, when a sale is cancelled, can the buyer always go back? Or can he go back only in the time it takes to show the item to a merchant or to his relative?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא formally asks the open question that the earlier steps were already arguing about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that for an overcharge of exactly one-sixth the buyer has only a short time to complain. The question is whether that same time limit also applies when the overcharge is so big (more than one-sixth) that the whole sale is cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked by the scholars (an open question)
Cancellation of the sale (when the overcharge is more than one-sixth)
He can always go back on the deal, with no time limit
Within the time it takes to show the item to a merchant or a relative

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:
Cancellation of the sale according to the Rabbis,
can one always go back,
or perhaps only within the time it takes to show it
to a merchant or to his relative?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: בִּטּוּל מִקָּח לְרַבָּנַן, לְעוֹלָם חוֹזֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally states the open question that steps 4-6 were already trying to prove.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether ביטול מקח under the רבנן has no time limit or is limited to the time needed to show the item to a merchant or relative.

steps.title: If both have the same time limit, what is the difference?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the second option: if a cancelled sale also has only the short time limit, there seems to be no difference between exactly one-sixth and more than one-sixth.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say it is only within the time to show it to a merchant or his relative, then what difference is there between an overcharge of one-sixth and an overcharge of more than one-sixth?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the option that a cancelled sale has only a short time limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Exactly one-sixth already has the short time limit. If more than one-sixth also has that same limit, it looks like the רבנן made two categories that work the same way, which would be strange.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (if you pick this side)

phrases.english: And if you say
it is only within the time to show it to a merchant or his relative,
what difference is there between one-sixth
and more than one-sixth?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר בִּכְדֵי שֶׁיַּרְאֶה לַתַּגָּר אוֹ לִקְרוֹבוֹ, מָה אִיכָּא בֵּין שְׁתוּת לְיָתֵר עַל שְׁתוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second side of the question in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The option that ביטול מקח is limited to the time to show a merchant or relative.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both one-sixth and more than one-sixth have the same time limit, the two categories seem to be the same.

steps.title: Who can back out is the difference
steps.stepSummary: There is still a difference: at exactly one-sixth only the cheated side has a claim, while above one-sixth both sides can back out.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference: with one-sixth, only the one who was cheated can go back, while with more than one-sixth, both can go back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that the two categories still work differently, even with the same time limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is not about how long, but about who has the right. At one-sixth only the cheated side has a claim. Above one-sixth the whole sale is cancelled, so even the side who gained can back out.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that 'both can go back' gives the cheater an unfair advantage. Since the sale is cancelled, it is simply not a sale, so either side may undo it.

phrases.english: There is a difference:
for with one-sixth,
only the one who was cheated can go back,
while with more than one-sixth,
both can go back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא: דְּאִילּוּ שְׁתוּת – מִי שֶׁנִּתְאַנָּה חוֹזֵר
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the two categories by who has the right, not by how long.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The only difference between the categories would be the time limit, so a shared time limit would erase the difference.
steps.terutzMaskana: At one-sixth only the cheated side may claim; above one-sixth both sides may back out.

steps.title: Proof from the merchants going back to the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove the short-time option from the משנה: the merchants of לוד went back to the רבנן, which only makes sense if the רבנן limit cancellation to a short time.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the answer? Come and hear: 'They went back to the words of the חכמים.' It makes sense if, for the רבנן, cancellation is only within the time to show a merchant or relative, while רבי טרפון gives the whole day. That is why they went back. But if for the רבנן one can always cancel, why did they go back? רבי טרפון's view is better for them, since he calls it only אונאה, for the whole day and no more!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer its question using the end of the משנה, where the merchants changed their minds and went back to the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture an overcharge between one-sixth and one-third. רבי טרפון calls it אונאה, which can be claimed for the whole day only. If the רבנן allowed cancellation forever, the merchants would lose by going back to the רבנן. So they must have gone back because the רבנן give only a short time.

keyTerms.meaning: They went back to the words of the Sages
It works well if you say

phrases.english: What is the answer?
Come and hear:
"They went back to the words of the Sages."
phrases.notes: This is the end of the משנה: the merchants of לוד first liked רבי טרפון's ruling, then switched back.

phrases.english: It works well if you say
that cancellation of the sale according to the Rabbis
is only within the time to show it to a merchant or his relative,
and according to Rabbi Tarfon, the whole day,
that is why they went back.
But if you say
that with cancellation under the Rabbis one can always go back,
why did they go back?
Rabbi Tarfon's view suits them better,
since he treats these cases as overcharge
phrases.notes: He means an overcharge between one-sixth and one-third, which the רבנן call a cancelled sale.

phrases.english: for the whole day and no more!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי? תָּא שְׁמַע, חָזְרוּ לְדִבְרֵי חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle the question of step 7 using the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That ביטול מקח under the רבנן is limited to the time to show a merchant or relative.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's report that the merchants of לוד went back to the words of the חכמים.

steps.title: Cancelled sales are rare
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected: cancelled sales rarely happen, so the merchants did not base their choice on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Cancellation of a sale is not common.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from the merchants in just three words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Big overcharges that cancel a sale do not happen often. So the merchants were thinking about the common cases of smaller overcharges, where the רבנן's short time limit helps them more than רבי טרפון's whole day. Their going back proves nothing about cancelled sales.

phrases.english: Cancellation of a sale is not common.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the merchants going back.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the merchants weighed the rare case of a cancelled sale; in fact they cared about the common cases.

steps.title: רבא's final הלכה on overcharging
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules: under one-sixth the sale stands, over one-sixth the sale is cancelled, exactly one-sixth the overcharge is returned, and both claims must be made within the time to show a merchant or relative.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said, the הלכה is: less than one-sixth, the sale is final. More than one-sixth, the sale is cancelled. Exactly one-sixth, the buyer keeps the item and the overcharge is given back. And both of these only within the time to show it to a merchant or his relative.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the final הלכה, following the רבנן, and settles the open question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא sets out three levels of overcharge. His last words, 'both this and that,' answer the question of step 7: even a cancelled sale can be undone only within the short checking time, not forever.
steps.whatToRemember: Under one-sixth: the sale stands. Exactly one-sixth: the sale stands and the extra money is returned. Over one-sixth: the sale is cancelled. For both of the last two, the claim must be made within the time it takes to show the item to a merchant or relative.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical הלכה of אונאה, and it closes the open question: there is no 'forever' for a cancelled sale.

phrases.english: Rava said: The halacha is:
less than one-sixth, the sale is final;
more than one-sixth, the sale is cancelled;
exactly one-sixth, he acquires it, and the overcharge is given back;
and both this and that,
phrases.notes: He means both cancelling the sale and getting the overcharge back.

phrases.english: only within the time to show it to a merchant or his relative.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof was rejected, רבא settles the question with a final ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The halacha follows the רבנן's three levels, and both cancellation and return of the overcharge are limited to the time needed to show the item to a merchant or relative.

steps.title: A ברייתא matches רבא's three-level ruling
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא in the name of רבי נתן gives the same three levels of overcharging that רבא ruled.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא agrees with רבא. If the overcharge is less than one-sixth, the sale stands. If it is more than one-sixth, the sale is cancelled. If it is exactly one-sixth, the sale stands but the overcharge is paid back. This is רבי נתן's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing רבא just ruled, as support for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's ruling in step 12 had three levels: under, over, and exactly one-sixth. This ברייתא of רבי נתן lists the very same three levels with the very same results, so רבא is not inventing anything new.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with him, agreeing with him
The sale goes through and is final

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא in line with רבא:
Overcharging of less than one-sixth: the sale is acquired.
More than one-sixth: the sale is cancelled.
Exactly one-sixth: he has acquired it, and the overcharge is given back,
These are the words of רבי נתן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that supports רבא's ruling from step 12.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling on the three levels of overcharging
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating רבי נתן's view

steps.title: A cheated seller has the upper hand, and both claims share one time limit
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה הנשיא says a cheated seller may choose to take back his item or get the overcharge returned. The ברייתא ends by saying both claims must be made within the time to show a merchant or relative.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה הנשיא says: the seller has the upper hand. If he wants, he can say to the buyer, 'Give me back my item,' or 'Give me back what you cheated me out of.' Both of these claims can only be made within the time it takes to show the item to a merchant or a relative.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a second opinion, from רבי יהודה הנשיא, about a seller who was cheated. Then it ends with the time limit for making a claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה הנשיא gives the cheated seller a choice: cancel the sale or keep it and take back the extra money. The closing line, that both claims have the same short time limit, is exactly רבא's last point in step 12. This is the second way the ברייתא supports רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: The seller has the upper hand; he gets to choose
My item, the thing I sold
What you cheated me out of

steps.confusionAlert: 'Upper hand' here means the cheated seller gets to choose what happens. It does not mean the seller is the one who did the cheating.

phrases.english: רבי יהודה הנשיא says:
The seller has the upper hand,
phrases.notes: He is talking about a seller who was the one cheated.

phrases.english: if he wants, he says to him: 'Give me my item,'
or 'Give me what you cheated me out of.'
And both this claim and that claim are only within the time
that it takes to show it to a merchant or to his relative.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a second opinion and the closing time-limit line that supports רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cheated seller may choose between cancelling the sale and getting the overcharge back, and either claim must be made within the time to show a merchant or relative.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא supports רבא twice: in the three levels of overcharging, and in the one short time limit for both cancelling and getting money back.

steps.title: The time limit applies only to the buyer
steps.stepSummary: Going back to the משנה's time limit, רב נחמן says it applies only to a buyer, while a seller can always back out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Until when may he return it?' רב נחמן said: They only taught this about a buyer. But a seller can always back out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה about how long one may return an item, and רב נחמן explains that the short deadline is only for the buyer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer can show the item to a merchant or relative right away, so he finds out quickly if he was cheated. רב נחמן teaches that a seller is not limited by this deadline at all and may always back out.
steps.whyThisMatters: It means the short deadline is not one rule for everyone. The seller's right to back out has no time limit.

phrases.english: The משנה said: 'Until when is one allowed to return it?' and so on.
רב נחמן said:
They only taught this about a buyer,
but a seller can always back out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לוֹקֵחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section on the משנה's time limit, after finishing with רבא's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The short time limit to back out applies only to the buyer. A seller may always back out.

steps.title: Trying to prove רב נחמן from the merchants of לוד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the משנה's story of the merchants going back to the חכמים supports רב נחמן, and begins to explain why.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say the משנה supports him? It says the merchants went back to the words of the חכמים. Now, if you say that a seller can always back out, that makes sense...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a proof for רב נחמן from the משנה's story of the merchants of לוד. The explanation begins here and continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The merchants of לוד were sellers, and they chose to go back to the חכמים' rule. If under the חכמים the deadline only limits buyers while sellers can always back out, that rule was good for the merchants, which explains their choice. The גמרא is starting to build this argument here.
